description: Saskatoon is Canada's only city actively collecting urban wildlife data.
Project uses 30 cameras to study urban wildlife habitats.
City hopes to dedicate staff time for long-term project coordination.

chips.text: Received as information
Wild About Saskatoon, the University, and Naturalized Parks are project partners.
Wild About Saskatoon thanked the committee for past support and future commitment.
Project aims to understand urban wildlife needs and reduce human-wildlife conflict.

speakers.name: Candace Savage
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Saskatoon's Urban Wildlife Information Network
said: Thanked council for supporting the Urban Wildlife Information Network project.
Funding helped maintain UWIN membership, replace equipment, and improve efficiency.
Hopes for continued commitment to this important scientific basis for wildlife management.

description: Saskatoon reviews Dutch Elm Disease and emerald ash borer prevention.
Public education includes radio announcements on pruning bans.

chips.text: Received as information
Councillor requested a heat map of removed elm trees; staff noted DED is city-wide.
Local residents can protect their own trees from emerald ash borer.
Dutch Elm Disease is now city-wide; emerald ash borer detected in Vancouver.

description: Committee will review a Bird Safe Saskatoon proposal for City Hall.
Proposal seeks up to $5,400 for deterrents and evaluation.

chips.text: Received as information
City Hall is one of Saskatoon's worst buildings for bird collisions.
Taxpayers could fund $50,000 for full north side window treatment.
Toronto's 2007 bird-friendly guidelines inspired similar North American standards.
Bird Safe Saskatoon presented a petition with 500 signatures.
Failure to comply with bird protection laws can result in lawsuits.
Bird collisions kill 16-42 million birds annually in Canada.
City facilities staff committed to installing pilot project materials.

description: Proposed digital sign rules address brightness, operating hours.
New setbacks would protect homes, natural areas.
Signs near sensitive areas would power off nightly.

chips.text: Received as information
Councillor questioned if revenue-neutral sign regulations serve companies or citizens.
360 citizens provided feedback on digital sign regulations.
Councillor suggested earlier shutdown and later restart for signs than staff proposed.
Existence of a comprehensive written dark sky policy remains unclear.
Light pollution abatement committee advocated for a master lighting plan.
Digital signs contribute to light pollution, impact migratory birds, and increase energy use.
Staff will refine recommendations using feedback before early 2026 approval.
